questions.q: Tell me about an Excel sheet or report you built or kept up in a past job or course. What data was in it, who used it, and what did you do each day or week?
questions.looks_for: Names a real sheet with real columns and users, describes their own part (entry, formulas, cleanup, sharing), and shows regular, careful work.

questions.q: Describe a time you used Excel to save time or fix a mistake in data. What was the problem and what changed after your work?
questions.looks_for: A specific problem (duplicates, wrong totals, manual copying), the steps or functions used, and a clear result like hours saved or errors caught.

questions.q: When would you use VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP, and what common mistakes make it give wrong or missing results?
questions.looks_for: Explains looking up a value from another table by a key; mentions exact vs approximate match, extra spaces, numbers stored as text, or the key column not being first for VLOOKUP.

questions.q: What is a pivot table, and how would you use one to show a manager total sales by month and by branch?
questions.looks_for: Describes summarising a big table without formulas; drags month/branch into rows or columns and sales into values as sum; mentions refreshing when data changes.

questions.q: What is the difference between a relative and an absolute cell reference, and when does it matter while copying a formula?
questions.looks_for: Relative changes when copied, absolute with $ stays fixed; gives an example like a fixed GST rate or target cell used by many rows.

questions.q: Your manager needs a stock report in one hour, but the data from two branches has different date formats and some duplicate rows. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Stays calm, keeps a copy of raw data, fixes date formats, removes duplicates carefully, checks totals against the source, and tells the manager of any doubt before the deadline.

questions.q: Why do you want this office assistant job, when can you join (please say your notice period), and what monthly salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
